Hi XXX -- glad you are trying it out.

That problem description, though, is very vague -- in general you will have to quote at least the command and the resulting error in order for someone to help you.

But, you can check:

1. Your working directory (wd), whether you have successfully set R to use the wd (setwd command), and whether or not you can write any files to it ("write permission", I don't know how it works in Windows).

2. Whether the "save" command works for anything else (you can save any R variable with "save").

3. Also perhaps:

trfn = np(paste(addslash("D:/biogeobears_XXX"), "finaltree5.newick", sep=""))
change to -->
trfn = "D:/biogeobears_XXX/finaltree5.newick

geogfn=np(paste(addslash("D:/biogeobears_XXX"), "geography.data", sep=""))
change to -->
geogfn="D:/biogeobears_XXX/geography.data"

4. Check if you need forward or backwards slashes for referring to files in your version of Windows. Older versions of windows needed \ instead of / in file paths, and in R paths this had to be written as \\ because \ was a special character.

The np and addslash commands in the example script are mostly useful for the default example files, although np (short for normalizePath) can convert between Mac and Windows slashes depending on the operating system.

Cheers!
Nick
